description:
Hi! We are Computer Engineering Undergraduates from University of Bohol! We have done projects with Machine Vision and Game Development combined. Combining our love for space and programming will be perfect for this challenge.

We designed the game exactly for young learners, easy to understand but still informative using NASA data/research links!

We are only a two man team, making the project in our free time. But rest assured this is NASA worthy! A huge shoutout to the Philippines!
summary:
Three Roles, Two Worlds: Outpost Odyssey is an educational mission game where students choose to be an engineer, botanist, or pilot and help establish an outpost on the Moon or Mars. Players complete interactive mission tasks involving power, life support, food production, radiation safety, and navigation. Their choices change the outpost’s resources and can determine whether the crew survives or the mission fails.

By turning spaceflight trade-offs into hands-on challenges, the game helps young learners understand why astronauts and mission teams must plan carefully and work together. It makes complex ideas about living beyond Earth engaging, accessible, and memorable, and invites students to think like the people who will shape future exploration.
details:
We made Outpost Odyssey, a space mission game for younger learners. Players choose to be an engineer, botanist, or pilot, then prepare for a trip to the Moon or Mars. They explore a 3D spacecraft and outpost and complete tasks involving power, air, food, water, radiation, and navigation.

The tasks show how one decision can affect the crew and the mission. If players use supplies poorly or miss an important check, the crew may be at risk. We wanted students to learn that living in space takes planning and teamwork, while still making the experience fun to play.

We built the game in Godot 4.4 with GDScript and 3D assets. While developing it, we considered how to make instructions clear for kids, keep the science grounded in NASA research, and show the consequences of players’ choices.
